candidates.source_name: ČNB – CERTIS (systém mezibankovního platebního styku) – hub
candidates.why_relevant: Landing hub of the Czech national RTGS/clearing system operated by the central bank. Aggregates system description, rulebook, fee schedule, participant lists (PDF+CSV), instant-payment sub-scheme and the contact-payments register. This is the single authoritative operator page for the rails every CZ bank settles on, and version-numbered participant lists make bank entry/exit machine-detectable.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled HTTP GET + HTML diff of the hub page; watch for participant-list version increments (seznam_certis_NN.csv) and new fee-schedule PDFs.

candidates.source_name: ČNB – CERTIS statistické údaje (+ ARAD dataset D458)
candidates.why_relevant: Monthly and annual CERTIS transaction counts and values (bn CZK). The page itself renders PNG charts but explicitly points to the ČNB ARAD time-series database, set D458, updated monthly — the machine-readable route to national clearing volumes. Core denominator for any CZ payments market sizing.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Pull time series from ARAD set D458 monthly (ARAD is a JavaScript SPA — needs a headless browser or its underlying JSON endpoint); fall back to scraping the chart page for release-date detection.

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Seznam účastníků systému CERTIS (CSV/PDF, versioned)
candidates.why_relevant: Machine-readable register of every direct CERTIS participant with bank codes and effective dates, published as numbered versions (v61 effective 2026-07-01, v62 effective 2026-09-01) plus a change-history PDF. The cleanest structured signal of a bank/PSP entering or leaving Czech clearing.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Direct file GET on a monthly cron; hash-compare successive versions and also probe seznam_certis_{N+1}.csv to catch the next version early.

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Okamžité platby (Czech instant payments scheme in CERTIS)
candidates.why_relevant: Operator-side page for the Czech instant-payment rail (live since end-2018). Publishes adoption share of interbank transfers, roll-out milestones and the EU euro instant-payment obligations (receiving mandatory Jan-2027, sending Jul-2027) plus batch-payment plans. Earliest public signal of rail-level change for CZ banks and merchants.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly HTML fetch + text diff; extract the adoption-share table and milestone dates.

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Seznam účastníků okamžitých plateb
candidates.why_relevant: Which Czech banks are actually live on instant payments, with a companion change-history file. Distinguishes CERTIS membership from instant-payment readiness — the practical measure of rail coverage for merchants and A2A payment products.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly PDF GET + text extraction; diff participant roster against previous snapshot.

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Registr pro platby na kontakt (RPK) – popis a seznam účastníků
candidates.why_relevant: Czech proxy-lookup register mapping mobile numbers to accounts, run alongside CERTIS. Underpins phone-number A2A payments — a direct competitive vector against card rails. Participant list and change history published.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly HTML + PDF fetch; diff participant roster.

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Národní fórum pro platby (National Payments Forum)
candidates.why_relevant: Multi-stakeholder platform created by ČNB in June 2026 with working groups on instant payments and payment-fraud prevention, meeting roughly quarterly. Where scheme-level CZ decisions get pre-negotiated between PSPs, payment users and public authorities — a forward-looking signal ahead of formal announcements. Currently thin on published material (one keynote PDF, one meeting notice), so value is in monitoring it as it fills up.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly HTML diff for new agendas, minutes and working-group outputs; contact address platebniforum@cnb.cz is listed publicly for participation requests.

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Oversight (dohled nad tržní infrastrukturou / PFMI hodnocení)
candidates.why_relevant: Describes ČNB's oversight of CERTIS and the SKD securities system against CFMI/PFMI principles, and states assessments were completed in 2023 (CERTIS previously 2016; SKD previously 2018). Confirms an assessment cadence worth tracking even though the assessment documents themselves are not linked from this page.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Low-frequency (quarterly) HTML diff; escalate if a downloadable assessment report ever appears.

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Digitální peníze centrálních bank (CBDC)
candidates.why_relevant: ČNB's public position and work on central bank digital currency, i.e. the potential future rail that would sit beside CERTIS and card schemes. Low-frequency but high-consequence for long-run rail strategy.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly HTML diff.

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Tiskové zprávy (central bank press releases)
candidates.why_relevant: Where CERTIS/instant-payment/infrastructure announcements are formally released before or alongside the topic pages. Needs topic filtering (payments vs monetary policy vs supervision) to stay in this cell's scope.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Weekly listing scrape with keyword filter (CERTIS, okamžité platby, platební styk, karty, podvody).

candidates.source_name: Visa Czech Republic – Newsroom / tiskové zprávy
candidates.why_relevant: Visa's Czech-market press releases in Czech: contactless and mobile-payment shares among Czech consumers, tokenisation milestones, cross-border/travel spending behaviour, acquisitions. The scheme's own framing of CZ market data — earliest public scheme-level signal. Note the URL path is English (/about-visa/) while content is Czech; the Czech-looking path /o-visa/tiskove-centrum.html returns 404, and individual releases sit under /o-spolecnosti-visa/newsroom/press-releases.NNNNNNN.html.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Weekly listing scrape of the newsroom page, then fetch each press-releases.NNNNNNN.html detail page; treat scheme-published statistics as marketing-framed and tag as vendor-sourced.

candidates.source_name: Mastercard Česká republika – Tiskové centrum
candidates.why_relevant: Mastercard's Czech-language press centre — the counterpart to Visa CZ for contactless share, tokenisation, wallet and merchant-acceptance announcements. Returned HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and a browser-UA curl, which is characteristic of Akamai/edge bot defence rather than a dead page; the domain is still linked as live from Czech trade sites. Treat as bot-defended-but-live and unverified.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Headless browser with realistic fingerprint, or rely on the SBK/CardMag mirror archive of Mastercard TZ PDFs (see aktuality.bankovnikarty.cz) as a fallback ingestion path.
candidates.observed_blocker: HTTP 403 Forbidden on https://www.mastercard.cz/cs-cz/o-nas/tiskove-centrum.html via both WebFetch and curl with a desktop Chrome user-agent; body not returned. Same 403 on the Czech interchange-fee page.

candidates.source_name: Mastercard global newsroom – press releases
candidates.why_relevant: Mastercard's global press feed, reachable when the Czech localised site is not. Carries Europe-wide scheme changes (tokenisation mandates, click-to-pay, instant-payment and open-banking moves) that propagate to CZ. Note: only /news/insights/, /news/perspectives/, /news/press/ and /news/terms-of-use/ were visible in the navigation — no country-level newsroom path was found, and www.mastercard.com/news/europe/cs-cz/ returns 403.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Weekly scrape with CZ/CEE keyword filter (Czech, Czechia, Prague, Central Europe); low CZ hit-rate expected, so use as a secondary feed.

candidates.source_name: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK) – statistiky českého kartového trhu
candidates.why_relevant: The Czech Bank Card Association publishes the only long-run, scheme-neutral CZ card dataset: quarterly and annual PDF + XLSX files covering cards in issue, cashless transaction counts/values, ATM withdrawals, cashback and e-commerce, with a consolidated history file back to 1989 and series from 2000-2026. Terminology and methodology manuals are published alongside. This is the reference series against which Visa/Mastercard marketing claims can be sanity-checked.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly GET of sbk_statistika_{N}kv_{YYYY}.pdf/.xlsx and the annual file; parse XLSX directly. Filenames follow a predictable pattern so the next quarter can be probed. Site is legacy static HTML in windows-1250 — decode explicitly.

candidates.source_name: SBK / CardMag – archiv tiskových zpráv Visa a Mastercard (aktuality.bankovnikarty.cz)
candidates.why_relevant: A long-running mirror archive holding several hundred PDF press releases (531 PDF links counted on the index) filed as TZ_VISA_*.pdf, TZ_MasterCard_*.pdf and similar, spanning roughly 2005 to August 2026. Because Mastercard's own Czech site is 403-blocked, this is the most practical ingestion route for historical and current Czech scheme press releases, and it preserves items the schemes later remove. Filenames encode date and issuer.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the index, harvest href list, download new TZ_*.pdf by filename date, OCR/parse text. Watch for malformed links on the referring pages (some hrefs are missing the '/' after the host, e.g. 'aktuality.bankovnikarty.czTZ_MasterCard_20-08-2026.pdf') — repair before fetching. Served over plain HTTP.

candidates.source_name: CardMag.cz – česká odborná platforma o platebních kartách
candidates.why_relevant: Czech card-industry trade publication, evidently run by the same circle as SBK (it mirrors the SBK statistics charts and the same TZ archive). Useful as a curated secondary feed that flags which scheme announcements the Czech industry itself considers notable, plus event coverage (Prague Payments Week, CardSession, Acquiring Day). Has an English mirror at /pages/eng/home_e.html.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Weekly HTML diff of the home page link set; deduplicate against the SBK archive since content largely overlaps. Legacy windows-1250 encoding; root URL is a meta-refresh redirect to /pages/cze/home.html.

candidates.source_name: Bank iD (Bankovní identita, a.s.) – Pro média
candidates.why_relevant: Press hub of the bank-owned national digital-identity operator. Publishes Czech-language press releases on public-sector and private use cases (land registry, school admissions, driving-licence renewal), plus downloadable factsheets carrying headline adoption numbers (cited as ~5.3m users, ~80% of the working-age population). Bank iD is the identity rail that CZ banks jointly own, so its releases signal where bank-issued identity is being monetised next. PR contact published on-page.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Weekly scrape of the media page and the linked factsheet PDFs (stable /files/ paths); extract adoption metrics from the annual factsheet.

candidates.source_name: Bank iD – Články / novinky (blog)
candidates.why_relevant: Higher-frequency companion to the press page: product launches, new relying parties, sector adoption commentary. Typically the first place a new Bank iD integration or feature is described in Czech.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Weekly listing scrape + article fetch; check for an RSS feed before falling back to HTML parsing.

candidates.source_name: Bank iD – Pro akcionáře (shareholder / general meeting materials)
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory shareholder page of the bank-owned operator. Currently thin — one general-meeting package (September 2026) as a ZIP — and notably it does NOT host an annual report or financial statements. Still worth monitoring because general-meeting materials disclose capital changes and new shareholder banks joining the identity scheme.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly HTML diff; download any new /files/*VH*.zip package and extract agenda/resolutions.

candidates.source_name: Bank iD – Developer portal (technická dokumentace)
candidates.why_relevant: Technical documentation and changelog for the Bank iD scheme. Spec/scope changes (new claims, new authentication levels, sign-service features) usually land here before any marketing announcement, making it a leading indicator of identity-rail capability shifts.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl of the changelog/release-notes section if present; diff the documentation tree.

candidates.source_name: Veřejný rejstřík a Sbírka listin – Bankovní identita, a.s. (IČO 09513817)
candidates.why_relevant: Because Bank iD does not publish an annual report on its own website, the statutory Collection of Deeds (Sbírka listin) at the Ministry of Justice is the only route to its audited financial statements, annual reports, shareholder structure and board changes. Registered office confirmed as Smrčkova 2485/4, Libeň, 180 00 Praha 8. The same registry serves any Czech-incorporated scheme or infrastructure entity in this cell.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Query by IČO, then walk the Sbírka listin document list and download new filings (accounting statements typically appear with a lag of 6-12 months). Note a new beta UI is being rolled out in parallel; pin the classic /ias/ui/ endpoints and re-test periodically. Beware shell expansion of the literal '$firma' segment in the URL.

candidates.source_name: ARES – Administrativní registr ekonomických subjektů (REST API)
candidates.why_relevant: Ministry of Finance registry with an open REST API that resolves Czech legal names to IČO and registered address — the entity-resolution layer for this cell (confirmed Bankovní identita, a.s. = IČO 09513817). Feeds the Sbírka listin lookup and disambiguates the many similarly named payment entities.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: POST to https://ares.gov.cz/ekonomicke-subjekty-v-be/rest/ekonomicke-subjekty/vyhledat with {"obchodniJmeno":"..."}; returns JSON with ico, obchodniJmeno, sidlo. Used successfully during this scout.

candidates.source_name: European Payments Council (EPC) – SEPA scheme owner
candidates.why_relevant: Owner and rulebook publisher for the SEPA schemes (SCT, SCT Inst, SDD Core, SDD B2B, Request-to-Pay, One-Leg Out) and of the register of scheme participants, in which Czech PSPs appear. Directly relevant to CZ because euro instant-payment obligations bite in 2027 and Czech banks adhering to SCT Inst show up in that register. Note the old domain www.epc-cep.eu now 301-redirects here; deeper paths (/what-we-do/sepa-payment-schemes, /document-library) returned 403 to automated fetches, which reads as bot defence rather than removal.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Headless browser for the document library and the register of participants; filter register extracts by country code CZ. Re-test the 403 paths — a single failure is not evidence they are gone.
candidates.observed_blocker: Root returns 200; https://www.europeanpaymentscouncil.eu/what-we-do/sepa-payment-schemes and /document-library both returned HTTP 403 to curl with a desktop Chrome user-agent. Legacy www.epc-cep.eu paths return 301 to the new root.

candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal – Payments statistics (PSS dataset)
candidates.why_relevant: Harmonised EU payments statistics including Czech Republic series on card payments, terminals, acceptance and payment-system throughput, compiled from ČNB reporting. Gives a cross-country comparable denominator that neither ČNB's Czech-only pages nor scheme marketing provide, and supports contactless/e-commerce share benchmarking against CEE peers.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the ECB SDMX/REST data API to pull PSS series filtered to reference area CZ; semi-annual/annual release cadence, so poll quarterly.

candidates.source_name: Česká bankovní asociace (ČBA) – Pro média
candidates.why_relevant: The Czech Banking Association is the collective voice of CZ banks on scheme-level topics (instant payments, SEPA migration, fraud prevention, identity) and is repeatedly cross-linked from Czech card-industry sites. Useful as a pointer to industry positions and to working groups that sit between the banks and CERTIS/Bank iD. Overlaps with a banking-association cell if one exists — deduplicate on ingest.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly scrape of the media section with payments keyword filter. Note https://cbaonline.cz/tiskove-zpravy returns a soft 404 page — use the /stranky/pro-media path from the site navigation instead, and re-derive paths from the homepage rather than guessing.

negative_findings.description: The session's WebSearch budget (200/200 calls) was already exhausted before this cell's first query was issued, so none of the assigned cs/en seed queries could actually be run. All discovery was performed instead by direct HTTP fetching of known operator domains, HTML link extraction, meta-refresh/redirect following and snowballing (ČNB nav -> CERTIS subpages; SBK homepage -> 531-PDF press archive, CardMag, ČBA; ARES API -> Sbírka listin). Consequently the queries_used fields are legitimately empty rather than fabricated.
negative_findings.result_summary: 0 web searches executed; ~40 direct fetches/status probes executed instead. Coverage of the cell's core actors was achieved, but long-tail recall that keyword search would have surfaced is likely missing.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Recall risk: sources that are not reachable by guessing a domain or by following a link from an already-known Czech payments site are systematically under-represented in this slice. Re-run the cell with search enabled to close the tail.

negative_findings.description: Mastercard's Czech localised estate refuses automated fetches. https://www.mastercard.cz/cs-cz/o-nas/tiskove-centrum.html and https://www.mastercard.cz/cs-cz/podnikatele/podpora/mezibankovni-poplatky.html both returned HTTP 403 with no body, to WebFetch and to curl with a desktop Chrome user-agent. https://www.mastercard.com/news/europe/cs-cz/ also returned 403.
negative_findings.result_summary: 403 on every Mastercard CZ path attempted. Not treated as dead: 403-with-no-body is the classic edge/bot-defence signature, and the domain is still linked as current from Czech trade sites (bankovnikarty.cz, cardmag.cz).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Mastercard is half of the duopoly this cell exists to track. Until a headless-browser collector is in place, Mastercard CZ coverage depends on the SBK/CardMag TZ_MasterCard_*.pdf mirror archive, which is a third-party mirror with unknown completeness.

negative_findings.description: Czech-looking localised paths on visa.cz do not exist: /o-visa/tiskove-centrum.html and /o-visa/novinky.html both return 404. The working Czech newsroom sits on an English path, https://www.visa.cz/about-visa/newsroom.html, while individual releases live under /o-spolecnosti-visa/newsroom/press-releases.NNNNNNN.html — a third path prefix.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two guessed Czech paths 404; the real newsroom (200, Czech-language content) was found by probing the English path. Three inconsistent path prefixes coexist on the same host.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any collector built on 'localise the path' heuristics will silently miss Visa CZ entirely and may record it as a dead source. Pin the discovered URLs and re-derive detail-page links from the listing rather than constructing them.

negative_findings.description: The acronym APMS (apms.cz), linked from the SBK homepage among payments-industry links, is NOT a payments body. It is the Asociace provozovatelů mobilních sítí — the Czech mobile network operators' association (O2, T-Mobile, Vodafone; IČO 75118891), concerned with telecom infrastructure.
negative_findings.result_summary: Fetched and confirmed off-topic. Excluded from candidates.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Noisy term for this cell: Czech payments sources cross-link telecom bodies (mobile payments context), and an unchecked acronym expansion would pollute the actor map. Flag APMS as excluded in the cell glossary.

negative_findings.description: No Czech-entity annual report, statutory financial statement or CZ-level investor-relations disclosure was found for Visa or Mastercard's Czech operations. Both schemes publish only marketing press releases locally; financial disclosure sits at group level. investor.visa.com and investor.mastercard.com both returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches (bot defence assumed, not verified as dead).
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero CZ-specific scheme financial disclosures located; group IR portals unreachable by automated fetch.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The 'annual reports / investor relations / earnings' topics in this run's scope cannot be satisfied from CZ scheme entities. For scheme economics, the run must fall back to group SEC filings (10-K/10-Q) or to interchange-fee regulatory disclosures, neither of which was located for CZ in this pass.

negative_findings.description: ČNB's oversight page states that PFMI-based assessments of CERTIS (2023, previously 2016) and of the SKD securities settlement system (2023, previously 2018) were completed, but publishes no link to the assessment documents themselves.
negative_findings.result_summary: Assessment existence confirmed in prose; assessment documents not located on the oversight page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The most substantive independent evaluation of the national clearing rail is referenced but not retrievable from the obvious location. Worth a targeted follow-up (ČNB annual report chapters, or an information request) rather than assuming the documents are unpublished.

negative_findings.description: Bankovní identita, a.s. publishes no výroční zpráva (annual report) or financial statements on bankid.cz. The /pro-akcionare/ page held exactly one artefact, a general-meeting ZIP for September 2026, and no shareholder-bank list.
negative_findings.result_summary: Self-published financial disclosure absent; statutory route via Sbírka listin (IČO 09513817, confirmed via ARES) is the only identified path.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Bank iD's economics and ownership structure — which banks hold what share of the national identity rail — are only obtainable with the 6-12 month lag of statutory filings, not from the operator's own site. Plan collection accordingly.

negative_findings.description: https://www.praguepaymentsweek.com/ (Czech payments industry conference, linked from both bankovnikarty.cz and cardmag.cz) timed out after 25 seconds with no response.
negative_findings.result_summary: Connection timeout, HTTP code 000. Recorded as unverified, not dead — a single timeout is not evidence of removal, and the site may simply be dormant between editions.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Conference programmes are a good pointer source for which scheme and infrastructure topics the Czech industry is prioritising, and for speaker-level actor mapping. Worth a retry from a different network before writing it off.

negative_findings.description: The ČNB ARAD statistical database (https://www.cnb.cz/arad/) is a JavaScript single-page application. A plain fetch returned only the shell 'ČNB ARAD' with no dataset content, so the structure of set D458 (CERTIS statistics, referenced by name from the CERTIS statistics page) could not be inspected, nor could the export formats or any API endpoint be confirmed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Dataset identifier D458 confirmed from the ČNB CERTIS page; dataset contents and export mechanics unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The machine-readable route to Czech clearing volumes is identified but not yet specified. A headless-browser or network-trace pass is needed to capture ARAD's underlying JSON endpoint before this can become an automated feed.

negative_findings.description: Guessed paths that do not exist and should not be re-probed: https://www.cnb.cz/cs/platebni-styk/okamzite-platby/ (404 — the real path is nested under /certis/), https://www.cnb.cz/cs/dohled-financni-trh/vykon-dohledu/dohled-nad-platebnimi-systemy/ (404 — oversight lives at /cs/platebni-styk/oversight/, an English word inside a Czech path), https://cbaonline.cz/tiskove-zpravy (soft 404 page), https://newsroom.mastercard.com/eu/ and /news/eu/en/ (404 — no country-level Mastercard newsroom found).
negative_findings.result_summary: Five plausible-looking paths confirmed non-existent; correct paths recorded in the candidate entries.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Documents the dead ends so a later run does not spend budget rediscovering them, and shows that ČNB mixes English slugs ('oversight') into Czech URL trees — path-localisation heuristics are unreliable on cnb.cz too.

negative_findings.description: Both bankovnikarty.cz and cardmag.cz emit malformed links to recent Mastercard press releases, missing the slash after the hostname: 'http://aktuality.bankovnikarty.czTZ_MasterCard_18-08-2026.pdf' and '...czTZ_MasterCard_20-08-2026.pdf'. The equivalent Visa link on the same pages is well-formed and fetches successfully (297 KB PDF).
negative_findings.result_summary: Two current Mastercard TZ links are unfetchable as published; the repaired form is the obvious fix but was not exercised.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A naive crawler will silently drop the newest Mastercard items from the very archive being used to work around the mastercard.cz 403 — compounding the Mastercard coverage gap. The collector must normalise these hrefs.

negative_findings.description: The SBK and CardMag estates are legacy static sites: the apex URLs serve only a meta-refresh redirect to /pages/czech/home.html and /pages/cze/home.html respectively, content is encoded in windows-1250 rather than UTF-8, the news archive is served over plain HTTP only, and pages carry FrontPage-era markup. WebFetch returned empty content for both apex URLs; only raw curl plus explicit iconv decoding worked.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both sites confirmed live (HTTP 200) and content-rich once the redirect and encoding are handled, but invisible to a standard fetch-and-parse pipeline.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single best CZ card-statistics series and the largest Czech scheme press archive would both be scored as empty or dead by a default collector. Encoding and meta-refresh handling must be explicit for this cell.

negative_findings.description: For the SEPA scheme layer (European Payments Council) and the comparative payments statistics layer (ECB Data Portal), no Czech-language version was found — both publish in English only. No Czech-language SEPA scheme rulebook or Czech national SEPA coordination portal was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: SEPA/EU-level sources are en-only in this slice; the cs-language SEPA layer is unfilled.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The run mandates cs coverage. If a Czech SEPA coordination body or Czech-language rulebook translation exists (plausibly hosted by ČBA), it was not found here and remains an open gap rather than a confirmed absence.

coverage_gaps.description: Non-duopoly card schemes operating in the Czech market were not scouted: American Express (americanexpress.com/czech, americanexpress.cz), Diners Club, JCB and Discover all appear as live links from the SBK/CardMag industry pages, indicating a CZ presence, but none was fetched or classified in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe each scheme's Czech-market presence and press channel, and check whether SBK's statistics break out non-Visa/Mastercard volumes. Start from the SBK homepage link block, which already lists all four.

coverage_gaps.description: Interchange-fee and scheme-fee disclosure pages for the Czech market — which the schemes are obliged to publish under the EU Interchange Fee Regulation — were not located. Two candidate paths were tried: visa.cz/about-visa/interchange.html and /o-spolecnosti-visa/interchange.html (both 404), and mastercard.cz/cs-cz/podnikatele/podpora/mezibankovni-poplatky.html (403).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate the current IFR disclosure URLs for Visa CZ and Mastercard CZ via on-site navigation (headless browser) rather than path guessing. These pages are the only public, quantitative, scheme-published pricing data for the CZ market.

coverage_gaps.description: Wallet and tokenisation operators sitting on top of the card rails in CZ — Apple Pay, Google Pay/Google Wallet, Garmin/Fitbit Pay, and the schemes' Click to Pay deployment (a Click to Pay page exists at visa.cz/business/consumers/click-to-pay.html) — were not scouted as sources. They are neither banks nor vendors, so like the schemes they risk falling between cells.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Decide explicitly whether wallet operators belong to this infrastructure cell or to a vendor cell, then scout their CZ-facing announcement channels. Tokenisation share is a headline metric in Visa CZ releases, so the two are already entangled.

coverage_gaps.description: This slice is heavily weighted to direct operator sources (ČNB, Visa, Mastercard, Bank iD) plus a small number of indirect/pointer sources. Aggregator and archive classes are thin: no news-aggregation feed, no RSS inventory, and no web-archive strategy was established for the schemes' press pages despite the demonstrated risk that scheme sites are bot-defended and that mirrors carry broken links.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a Wayback/archive.org capture strategy for visa.cz and mastercard.cz newsrooms, and inventory RSS/Atom feeds across all candidates (none was confirmed in this pass) so polling can move from HTML diffing to feeds where available.

coverage_gaps.description: Czech-language coverage is strong for ČNB, Visa CZ, Bank iD, SBK and CardMag. It is absent for the SEPA/EU layer, and no Slovak- or German-language comparator was scouted even though zbk.sk (the Slovak bank card association, the direct analogue of SBK) is linked from the SBK homepage and would provide a near-identical dataset for cross-border benchmarking.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: If cross-border comparison is in scope for later workstreams, scout zbk.sk as the Slovak mirror of SBK. Within CZ scope, hunt specifically for a Czech-language SEPA/instant-payment scheme description outside ČNB (likely ČBA-hosted).

coverage_gaps.description: Three of the highest-value targets in this cell (mastercard.cz, the EPC document library and register of participants, and the ČNB ARAD database) are all unreachable by plain HTTP fetching — two via 403 bot defence, one via a JavaScript SPA. No headless-browser collection capability was exercised or confirmed available during this scout.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Stand up a headless-browser collector with a realistic fingerprint before the collection phase for this cell, and validate it against exactly these three targets. Without it, roughly a third of the cell's critical/high-priority sources cannot be ingested and would be misrecorded as dead.

coverage_gaps.description: Because zero keyword searches could be run, discovery was confined to what could be reached by domain guessing and link-following from a small seed set. Entire plausible source types for this cell were therefore never tested: Czech payments trade newsletters, LinkedIn/X accounts of the schemes' CZ country managers (SBK's own X account @SdruzeniK was seen but not assessed), scheme-sponsored CZ consumer research reports, and tender/procurement notices for national payment infrastructure.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell with the WebSearch budget restored, executing the assigned cs and en seed queries plus snowballed terms, and treat the present slice as a verified core rather than a complete map.

brief: The Czech scheme-and-rails layer splits cleanly into three publisher types. First, the ČNB is an unusually generous operator-of-record: CERTIS gets its own portal with a rulebook, versioned participant lists in CSV, a monthly statistics series exposed through ARAD set D458, a dedicated instant-payments page carrying adoption share and the 2027 euro-instant deadlines, the proxy-lookup Registr pro platby na kontakt, and — new since June 2026 — a National Payments Forum whose instant-payments and fraud working groups should become the earliest forward signal in this cell. Second, the card schemes publish only marketing-grade Czech press releases and no CZ-level financials, and Mastercard's Czech estate is 403-blocked to automated fetching while Visa's Czech newsroom hides behind an English URL path; the practical workaround for both is the Sdružení pro bankovní karty estate (bankovnikarty.cz / cardmag.cz), a legacy windows-1250 static site that quietly holds the only long-run scheme-neutral CZ card dataset (quarterly XLSX back to 2000, history to 1989) plus a 531-file archive of Visa and Mastercard press releases running to August 2026. Third, Bank iD is well covered for news and adoption factsheets but publishes no annual report, so its ownership and economics are reachable only through the statutory Sbírka listin under IČO 09513817. The binding constraint on this slice is tooling, not sources: the session's search budget was exhausted before any query ran, so everything here was found by direct fetch and snowballing, and three critical targets (mastercard.cz, the EPC document library, ARAD) will need a headless browser before they can be collected at all.
